headline: High: firecrawl’s broad egress and API-key handling can leak data or cascade bad outputs when paired with a prompt-leakage agent, while shared-write conflicts are less evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: firecrawl ingests web content and exposes MCP-compatible/API surfaces, so attacker-controlled pages can reach its outputs. system_prompts_leaks is explicitly about prompt leakage, making an instruction-hijack pathway plausible if its outputs are fed into firecrawl or vice versa. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF firecrawl output is copied into system_prompts_leaks prompts or vice versa
IF either agent parses untrusted page text as instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following on fetched content
Strip or quote web text before passing between agents
Use a fixed prompt template with delimiters
Review one sample interaction for prompt markers
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all transferred content

B_data_leakage.rationale: firecrawl touches API keys and has broad network egress, so sensitive content can leave the local boundary. system_prompts_leaks is a prompt-leakage target, which increases the chance that secrets or system prompts are exposed if firecrawl fetches or forwards them. The pair lacks a documented isolation boundary, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF firecrawl processes pages or inputs containing API keys or other secrets
IF outputs from either agent are sent to a third-party backend without redaction
mitigations: Remove secrets from inputs before crawling

C_capability_conflict.rationale: firecrawl supports multiple instances and has API/CLI surfaces, but system_prompts_leaks shows no write or network capability. There is no documented shared mutable resource, so direct write-write conflict is not evidenced. The main risk is limited to operational contention if an external orchestrator shares state.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator points both agents at the same mutable workspace
IF firecrawl instances are run concurrently against the same output directory
mitigations: requires-engineering: add lock files around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: firecrawl can generate scraped facts and markdown that another agent may treat as authoritative. system_prompts_leaks is a prompt-leakage-oriented repo, so if it consumes firecrawl output without verification, errors or malicious content can cascade into downstream analysis. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF system_prompts_leaks consumes firecrawl output as trusted input
IF no verification step checks scraped facts before reuse
mitigations: Require source URLs alongside extracted claims
Compare outputs against a second fetch
requires-engineering: implement confidence scoring on transferred facts

E_compliance.rationale: firecrawl explicitly handles API keys and broad egress, which can create retention or residency issues for sensitive web content. system_prompts_leaks is source-available and not runnable, so it is not the main compliance driver; the compliance concern is primarily firecrawl’s handling of sensitive data. Because the other agent lacks relevant residency or retention fields, it is not cited beyond the pair context.
conditions: IF regulated data is crawled through firecrawl
IF logs or upstream APIs retain fetched content beyond policy
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in crawl targets
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
